_meta.note: CT-D public_justice q0 F->T, Principal ruling 2026-10-08 06:53 (MBP-1008-AM): the mixed CT platform text (Criminal Legal Reform plank also decries over-policing) resolves TRUE on its plank backing law enforcement pay, healthcare and retirement, the same precedent as MA-D ("Better resources to support law enforcement") and MN-D ("strong law enforcement policies") on 2026-10-07.

0.note: kind: party_platform_state. Connecticut Democratic Party Platform 2026 (ctdems.org/platform states the platform was adopted in 2026 by the Democratic State Convention), section Criminal Legal Reform (page slug is mislabeled lgbtqia-rights; re-fetched 2026-10-08 HTTP 200), fetched 2026-10-08: "We recognize the sacrifices that law enforcement, firefighters and other public safety personnel make to keep us safe. We support efforts to increase occupational mortality for public safety personnel and ensure that they have a good pay, healthcare and retirement." (The word mortality is verbatim as published.) The same plank also supports reform for communities "that have been overpoliced and over sentenced". State platform governs where one is online (Principal ruling 2026-10-07). Principal ruling 2026-10-08: the mixed CT platform text resolves TRUE because the plank backs pay, healthcare and retirement for law enforcement, so the cell follows the state answer (was False on the national 2024 DNC platform only); same precedent as MA-D and MN-D on 2026-10-07. The CT platform does not adopt or reject the national platform.
